chunks: When a speck of dust or impurity is removed from you, say: 'May God remove from you what you dislike.'
When your brother says to you upon leaving the bathhouse: 'May your bath and water be fragrant,' say: 'May God grant you goodness.'
When your brother says to you: 'May God greet you with peace,' say: 'And you, may God greet you with peace and settle you in the Abode of Permanence.'
Do not urinate on the pathway, nor defecate on it.
Ask after praising, so praise God, the Mighty and Majestic, then ask for your, then ask for your needs.
Exalt God, the Mighty and Majestic, and praise Him before seeking your needs.
O companion of supplication, do not ask for that which will not happen or is not permissible.
When a man congratulates you on a newborn boy, say: 'May God bless you in His gift, bring him to his prime, and grant you his goodness.'

When your brother returns from Mecca, kiss between his eyes, his mouth with which he kissed the Black Stone which the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) kissed, and the eye with which he looked at the House of God (the Mighty and Majestic), and kiss the place of his prostration and his face.

And when you congratulate him, say to him: 'May God accept your sacrifice, have mercy on your effort, compensate you for your expenses, and not make it the last of your covenant with His Sacred House.'
Beware of the lowly/foolish, for the lowly are those who do not fear God, the Mighty and Majestic. Among them are the killers of the Prophets, and among them are our enemies.

Indeed, God, Blessed and Exalted, looked to the earth and chose us, and chose for us a Shiah (followers), who support us, rejoice at our joy, grieve at our grief, and expend their wealth and lives for us. Those are from us and to us.

From the beginning of the Shiah, a servant commits a matter we forbade him from, and dies until he is tested with a calamity that purifies his sins, whether in wealth, or in children, or in his self, until he meets God, the Mighty and Majestic, and has no sin. And if something of his sins remains, it is made heavy upon him at his death.

The deceased of our Shiah is a sincere friend and a martyr, who was true to our command, loved for our sake, and hated for our sake, seeking thereby God, the Mighty and Majestic. He is a believer in God and His Messenger.

God, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And those who believe in God and His messengers - those are they who are the sincere (in faith) and the martyrs, with their Lord. For them is their reward and their light.'
The Children of Israel divided into seventy-two sects, and this Ummah will divide into seventy-three sects, one of which is in Paradise.
Whoever proclaims our secret, God will make him taste the bitterness of iron.
Circumcise your children on the seventh day, let not heat or cold prevent you, for it is purification for the body, and indeed the earth cries out to God from the urine of the uncircumcised.
Drunkenness is four types: drunkenness of drink, drunkenness of wealth, drunkenness of sleep, and drunkenness of kingship.
When one of you intends to sleep, let him place his right hand under his right cheek, for he does not know where he will wake from his sleep or not.
I love for the believer to apply depilatory cream (nurah) every fifteen days.

key_terms.قَذَاةٌ: Speck of dust or impurity removed from the body

ai.seo_question: What are the key etiquettes and ethical teachings of Imam Ali (AS) for daily Muslim life?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, this narration captures Imam Ali’s (AS) concise, aphoristic teachings delivered in a single session, reflecting the practical jurisprudence (*fiqh*) and spiritual ethics central to early Shia scholarship. The text bridges social etiquette (*adab*) with theological identity, emphasizing the distinct characteristics of the *Shi'a* through their loyalty to theocentric conduct and readiness for martyrdom. It serves as a foundational guide for integrating daily rituals, such as greeting and sleeping postures, with broader eschatological and communal principles.
